leftEvidence.title: David sits before the LORD and answers the promise

points.label: Action and response
points.left: David asks who he and his house are, speaks of God’s greatness and Israel’s redemption, and asks that the spoken word and house be established.
points.right: Campaigns against Philistines, Moab, Hadadezer, Syria, Edom, and others bring tribute and dedicated objects; the chapter closes with justice, officials, and David’s sons.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places promise becomes prayer without erasing David’s questions inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places military expansion and administrative order are narrated together inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 7:18–29 and 2 Samuel 8:1–18 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Ark, House, and Kingdom” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.
payload.tension: 2 Samuel 7:18–29 foregrounds promise becomes prayer without erasing David’s questions; 2 Samuel 8:1–18 foregrounds military expansion and administrative order are narrated together. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
